name: Bookmarks
description: A small shelf of links: paste an address, click it to open in your browser
author: Lattice

config.label: Order
config.help: Newest first keeps what you just saved on top; By name and By site are for when the shelf is full.

config.label: Show the site under each name
config.help: Turn it off for a one-line list that fits more links.

sections.title: Saving a link
items: Paste an address in the box at the top and press Enter.
You do not need the https:// part — github.com is saved as https://github.com/.
Only http and https links are accepted. file: and javascript: are refused, because they can read local files or run code.
Saving the same address twice just says it is already on the shelf — no duplicates.
Hover a row and click the × to remove it.

sections.title: Opening a link
items: Click a row (or press Enter on it) to open it in your default browser.
This needs the Open links permission. Without it the card says so instead of doing nothing.
In the browser preview there is no system browser to call, so opening only works in the desktop app.

sections.title: Naming a link
items: Hover a row and click the pencil, or press F2 on a focused row.
Enter or clicking anywhere else saves the name; Esc puts the old one back.
An empty name falls back to the site address, so a row is never nameless.

sections.title: One shelf, several windows
items: Every Bookmarks widget shows the same shelf — it is stored per widget, not per copy.
Add a link in one window and the other windows update right away.

sections.title: Order and density
items: The Order setting in the properties panel sorts by newest, by name, or by site.
Show the site under each name can be turned off for a denser one-line list.
The shelf holds up to 100 links.

sections.title: If it cannot save
items: The counter switches to Not saved when a write fails — usually a missing storage permission.
Hover it to see the reason. The list keeps working in memory until it can write again.

changes: First release: paste an address, press Enter, click a row to open it in your browser.
Rename a link with the pencil (or F2); empty names fall back to the site address.
Order by newest, name, or site; hide the site line for a denser list.
